Otherwise we replace each $u_ l$ by $u_ l/(2\| u_ l\| _{L^\infty (L)})-3/2$, which takes values in $[-2,-1]$ on $L$; by proposition 7.2.2 (3) this multiplies the left-hand side by $\prod _ l(2\| u_ l\| _{L^\infty (L)})^{-1}$. For each $a\in K$ choose $R_ a>0$ with $\overline{B(a,R_ a)}\subset \operatorname{Int}L$; finitely many of the balls $B(a,R_ a/2)$ cover $K$, and this choice depends only on $K$ and $L$. Hence it suffices to prove the following: for concentric balls $B'=B(a,R')$ and $B=B(a,R)$ with $R'<R$ and $\overline B\subset \operatorname{Int}L$, there is a constant $C$, depending only on $B'$, $B$, $L$, $n$ and $q$, such that \[  \int _{B'}|V|\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q\wedge \beta ^{n-q}\le C\| V\| _{L^1(L)}  \] whenever $u_1,\ldots ,u_ q$ are plurisubharmonic on $\Omega $ with values in $[-2,-1]$ on $L$. Step 2: a common collar. Put $\psi =|z-a|^2-R^2$ and $b=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi =\beta /\pi $, and choose $\delta >0$ with $\overline{B'}\subset \{ \psi <-\delta \} $. Replace each $u_ l$ by $\max \{ u_ l,A\psi \} $, where $A=2/\delta $; this function is plurisubharmonic on $\Omega $ (proposition 5.9.5 ). By ( 7.3.2 ), with $N=2$ and $U=\operatorname{Int}L$, it is unchanged on $\{ \psi <-\delta \} $, it equals $A\psi $ on the collar $V_0=\{ z\in \operatorname{Int}L:\psi (z)>-\delta /2\} $ of $\partial B$, and it takes values in $[-2,0)$ on $B$. Let $S=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q$ be the product of the modified functions. Put $\tau =\delta /4$ and $B_\tau =\{ \psi <-\tau \} $. Then $\overline{B'}\subset B_\tau $, and on the neighborhood $V_0$ of $\overline B\setminus B_\tau $ we have $S=(A\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi )^ q=A^ qb^ q$ by proposition 7.2.2 (1),(2). By lemma 2.5.1 (4) there is $\theta \in C^\infty _ c(B)$ with $0\le \theta \le 1$ and $\theta =1$ on a neighborhood of $\overline{B_\tau }$; the function $\chi =-\psi \theta $ is smooth, nonnegative, has compact support in $B$, and equals $-\psi $ on a neighborhood of $\overline{B_\tau }$. All these choices depend only on $B'$, $B$ and $L$. Step 3: smooth $V$ and $q\le n-1$. Suppose that $q\le n-1$ and that $V$ is smooth and plurisubharmonic on a neighborhood of $\overline B$ with $V\le 0$ on $B_\tau $. The signed measure $S\wedge b^{n-q-1}\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi $ has compact support in $B$. Splitting its integral against $V$ over $B_\tau $, where $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi =-b$, and over $B\setminus B_\tau \subset V_0$, where $S=A^ qb^ q$, we obtain \[  \begin{aligned}  \int _{B_\tau }(-V)S\wedge b^{n-q} & =\int _ B V S\wedge b^{n-q-1}\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi -A^ q\int _{B\setminus B_\tau }V b^{n-1}\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi \\ & =\int _ B\chi \, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}V\wedge S\wedge b^{n-q-1} -A^ q\int _{B\setminus B_\tau }V b^{n-1}\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi . \end{aligned}  \] The second equality holds because the first integral is $(VS\wedge b^{n-q-1})(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi )=\bigl (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(VS\wedge b^{n-q-1})\bigr )(\chi )$, and $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(VS\wedge b^{n-q-1})=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}V\wedge S\wedge b^{n-q-1}$ by ( 7.2.3 ), the current $S\wedge b^{n-q-1}$ being closed. The smooth form $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}V$ is closed, and it is strongly positive, since its coefficient matrix is positive semidefinite (proposition 5.9.2 ) and weak and strong positivity agree in bidegree $(1,1)$ (section 5.3 ); so by proposition 7.2.2 (4), with $T=1$ and $\gamma =\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}V$, the current $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}V\wedge S$ is the product $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}V$ with the closed positive base current $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}V$ of bidimension $(n-1,n-1)$. Choose a compact set $L'\subset B$ whose interior contains $\operatorname{Supp}\chi $. The first term is at most $\pi ^{q+1-n}\sup \chi $ times the mass of the trace measure of $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}V$ on $\operatorname{Supp}\chi $. Since the modified $u_ l$ take values in $[-2,0)$ on $B$, theorem 7.2.5 , applied to $\operatorname{Supp}\chi \subset \operatorname{Int}L'$, shows that the first term is at most $C\| \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}V\| _{L'}$, with $C$ depending only on $\chi $, $L'$, $n$ and $q$. Let $\chi '\in C^\infty _ c(B)$ satisfy $0\le \chi '\le 1$ and $\chi '=1$ on $L'$. Since $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}V\wedge \beta ^{n-1}\ge 0$, \[  \| \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}V\| _{L'}\le \int \chi '\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}V\wedge \frac{\beta ^{n-1}}{(n-1)!}=\int V\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi '\wedge \frac{\beta ^{n-1}}{(n-1)!}\le C\int _ B|V|\, \mathrm{d}V_{2n},  \] where $C$ bounds the coefficient of the smooth $(n,n)$-form $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi '\wedge \beta ^{n-1}/(n-1)!$. The collar term is bounded by the same quantity, because $b^{n-1}\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi $ has bounded smooth coefficients. Hence \[  \int _{B_\tau }(-V)S\wedge b^{n-q}\le C\int _ B|V|\, \mathrm{d}V_{2n}.  \] Step 4: general $V$ and $q\le n-1$. Let $V\in \mathrm{PSH}(\Omega )$, and choose $r_0>0$ with $2r_0<\operatorname {dist}(\overline B,\mathbb C^ n\setminus \operatorname{Int}L)$. The function $V$ is subharmonic (theorem 5.9.1 ). If $x$ lies within distance $r_0$ of $\overline B$, then $\overline{B(x,r_0)}\subset \operatorname{Int}L$, and the ball submean inequality of theorem 3.4.5 (2) gives \[  V(x)\le \frac1{|B(x,r_0)|}\int _{B(x,r_0)}V\, \mathrm dV_{2n}\le c_0\| V\| _{L^1(L)},\qquad c_0=|B(0,r_0)|^{-1};  \] put $c=c_0\| V\| _{L^1(L)}$. For $0<\varepsilon <r_0$ the regularization $V_\varepsilon =V*\rho _\varepsilon $ is smooth and plurisubharmonic on the neighborhood $\{ z:\operatorname {dist}(z,\overline B)<r_0\} $ of $\overline B$ (proposition 5.9.2 ), since this neighborhood lies in $\Omega _\varepsilon $. It satisfies $V_\varepsilon \le c$ on $\overline B$, since $V_\varepsilon (x)$ is an average of values of $V$ at points within distance $\varepsilon $ of $x$, and $\int _ B|V_\varepsilon |\, \mathrm{d}V_{2n}\le \int \rho _\varepsilon (y)\int _ B|V(x-y)|\, \mathrm dV_{2n}(x)\, \mathrm dV_{2n}(y)\le \| V\| _{L^1(L)}$ by Tonelli's theorem, since $B-y\subset L$ for $|y|\le \varepsilon $. Applying Step 3 to $V_\varepsilon -c$ gives \[  \int _{B_\tau }(c-V_\varepsilon )\, S\wedge b^{n-q}\le C\bigl (\| V\| _{L^1(L)}+c|B|\bigr )\le C'\| V\| _{L^1(L)}.  \] As $\varepsilon \downarrow 0$, the nonnegative functions $c-V_\varepsilon $ increase to $c-V$, by ( 3.4.13 ), so monotone convergence gives the same bound for $\int _{B_\tau }(c-V)\, S\wedge b^{n-q}$. Since $V\le c$ on $B_\tau $, we have $|V|\le (c-V)+c$ there, and the mass of $S\wedge b^{n-q}$ on $B_\tau $ is bounded by a constant depending only on $B'$, $B$, $n$ and $q$, by theorem 7.2.5 applied to $\overline{B_\tau }\subset B=\operatorname{Int}\overline B$, since the modified $u_ l$ take values in $[-2,0]$ on $\overline B$. Since $S$ coincides with the original product on $B'\subset B_\tau $, by locality, this proves the estimate of Step 1 for $q\le n-1$. By the finite cover and the normalizations of Step 1, the theorem holds for $q\le n-1$, in every dimension. Step 5: the case $q=n$. Consider $\mathbb C^{n+1}$ with coordinates $(z,w)$, the unit disc $\Delta \subset \mathbb C$, and the projection $p(z,w)=z$; let $\beta _ z$, $\beta _ w$ be the forms ( 5.2.8 ) in the variables $z$ and $w$, so that $\beta _ z+\beta _ w$ is the form $\beta $ of $\mathbb C^{n+1}$, and $\beta _ w=\mathrm dV_2(w)$. By proposition 5.9.3 , the functions $u_ l\circ p$ are locally bounded and plurisubharmonic on $\Omega \times \Delta $, and $V\circ p$ is plurisubharmonic there, since it is not identically $-\infty $ on any connected component $\Omega _0\times \Delta $ of $\Omega \times \Delta $. Let $\mu =\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ n$, a positive measure on $\Omega $. We claim that \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u_1\circ p)\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u_ n\circ p)\wedge (\beta _ z+\beta _ w)=\mu \otimes \mathrm{d}V_2.  \] If the $u_ l$ are smooth, then $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u_ l\circ p)=p^*\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ l$, so the product of these $n$ factors is the pullback $p^*\mu $ of the $(n,n)$-form $\mu =g\, \mathrm dV_{2n}$ (proposition 7.2.2 (1)). Its exterior product with $\beta _ z$ is $p^*(\mu \wedge \beta )=0$, since $\mu \wedge \beta $ has bidegree $(n+1,n+1)$ on $\mathbb C^ n$, and its exterior product with $\beta _ w$ is $g(z)\, \mathrm dV_{2n}(z)\wedge \mathrm dV_2(w)$, the density of $\mu \otimes \mathrm dV_2$. In general, let $u_{l,\varepsilon }=u_ l*\rho _\varepsilon $, which are smooth plurisubharmonic functions on $\Omega _{\varepsilon _0}$ for $\varepsilon <\varepsilon _0$, decreasing to $u_ l$ as $\varepsilon \downarrow 0$ (proposition 5.9.2 ). By theorem 7.3.7 , applied on $\Omega _{\varepsilon _0}\times \Delta $ to the functions $u_{l,\varepsilon }\circ p$, which decrease to $u_ l\circ p$, the left-hand sides for $u_{l,\varepsilon }$ converge weakly to the left-hand side for $u_ l$. By the same theorem on $\Omega _{\varepsilon _0}$, the measures $\mu _\varepsilon =\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{1,\varepsilon }\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{n,\varepsilon }$ converge weakly to $\mu $; hence $\mu _\varepsilon \otimes \mathrm dV_2\to \mu \otimes \mathrm dV_2$, because for a test function $\varphi $ on $\Omega _{\varepsilon _0}\times \Delta $ we have $\int \varphi \, \mathrm d(\mu _\varepsilon \otimes \mathrm dV_2)=\int \Phi \, \mathrm d\mu _\varepsilon $ with $\Phi (z)=\int _\Delta \varphi (z,w)\, \mathrm dV_2(w)$, a test function on $\Omega _{\varepsilon _0}$ (differentiate under the integral sign). Since $\varepsilon _0$ is arbitrary, the claim follows from the smooth case. Now apply the case already proved in dimension $n+1$, with $q=n\le (n+1)-1$, to the compact sets $\widetilde K=K\times \{ |w|\le 1/2\} $ and $\widetilde L=L\times \{ |w|\le 3/4\} $ in $\Omega \times \Delta $; note that $\widetilde K\subset \operatorname{Int}\widetilde L$. By the claim and Fubini's theorem, the left-hand side of the estimate for $V\circ p$ and the $u_ l\circ p$ is $\frac\pi 4\int _ K|V|\, \mathrm d\mu $, while $\| V\circ p\| _{L^1(\widetilde L)}=\frac{9\pi }{16}\| V\| _{L^1(L)}$ and $\| u_ l\circ p\| _{L^\infty (\widetilde L)}=\| u_ l\| _{L^\infty (L)}$. Hence the estimate holds in $\mathbb C^ n$ with the constant $\frac94C_{\widetilde K,\widetilde L,n}$, which depends only on $K$, $L$ and $n$. This proves the case $q=n$. $\square$ The base current in theorem 7.4.1 is $T=1$, and for a general closed positive current $T$ no such estimate holds, already for $q=0$. Let $n\ge 1$, let $H=\{ z_1=0\} \subset \mathbb C^ n$, and let $T=[H]$ be the current of integration of example 5.3.9 , a closed positive current of bidimension $(n-1,n-1)$. In the coordinates $z_2,\ldots ,z_ n$ of $H$, the restriction of $\beta $ to $H$ is the form ( 5.2.8 ) of $\mathbb C^{n-1}$, so $T\wedge \beta ^{n-1}/(n-1)!$ is Lebesgue measure on $H$. The function $V=\log |z_1|$ is plurisubharmonic (proposition 5.10.3 ), hence $\| V\| _{L^1(L)}<\infty $ for every compact $L$, but $V=-\infty $ on $H$. Therefore $\int _ K|V|\, T\wedge \beta ^{n-1}=\infty $ for the closed unit ball $K$, which meets $H$ in a set of positive Lebesgue measure on $H$. Definition 7.4.2 . E9E7C75396D2 Let $D\subset \mathbb {C}^ n$, $n\ge 1$, be a bounded open set. The Monge–Ampère capacity of a Borel set $E\subset D$ is \[  \operatorname {Cap}_ D(E)=\sup \left\{ \int _ E(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n: v\in \mathrm{PSH}(D),\  0\le v\le 1\right\} .  \] The functions $v$ in this supremum are called competitors for $\operatorname {Cap}_ D$. The outer capacity of an arbitrary set $A\subset D$ is \[  \operatorname {Cap}_ D^*(A)=\inf \{ \operatorname {Cap}_ D(G):A\subset G\subset D, \  G\text{ open}\} .  \] On a complex manifold we use these capacities in coordinate charts, taking for $D$ a bounded open set, usually a ball, which is relatively compact in the chart. Proposition 7.4.3 . 97EFDB6FDEE3 Let $D\subset \mathbb C^ n$ be a bounded open set. The set functions $\operatorname {Cap}_ D$ and $\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D$ are increasing with respect to inclusion and countably subadditive. Moreover: $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(K)<\infty $ for every compact $K\subset D$, and $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(E)=\sup \{ \operatorname {Cap}_ D(K):K\subset E\text{ compact}\} $ for every Borel set $E\subset D$; if $E_ j\subset D$ are Borel sets increasing to $E$, then $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(E_ j)\to \operatorname {Cap}_ D(E)$; there is a constant $C_ D$ such that $|E|\le C_ D\operatorname {Cap}_ D(E)$ for every Borel set $E\subset D$, where $|E|$ is Lebesgue measure; if $B\Subset D$ is a ball and $K\subset B$ is compact, there is a constant $C$ such that, for every Borel set $E\subset K$, \[  \operatorname {Cap}_ D(E)\le \operatorname {Cap}_ B(E) \le C\operatorname {Cap}_ D(E),  \] and the same inequalities hold for the outer capacities of arbitrary subsets of $K$; both capacities are invariant under biholomorphisms between bounded open sets: if $F\colon D\to D'$ is biholomorphic, then $\operatorname {Cap}_{D'}(F(E))=\operatorname {Cap}_ D(E)$ for Borel sets $E\subset D$ and $\operatorname {Cap}^*_{D'}(F(A))=\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(A)$ for arbitrary sets $A\subset D$. Proof. For each competitor $v$, the measure $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n$ is increasing and countably subadditive on Borel sets: $\int _{\bigcup _ jE_ j}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n\le \sum _ j\int _{E_ j}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n\le \sum _ j\operatorname {Cap}_ D(E_ j)$. Taking the supremum over $v$ gives the same properties for $\operatorname {Cap}_ D$. Outer capacity is increasing by definition. For countable subadditivity, given sets $A_ j$ with $\sum _ j\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(A_ j)<\infty $ and $\varepsilon >0$, choose open sets $G_ j\supset A_ j$ with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G_ j)<\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(A_ j)+\varepsilon 2^{-j}$; then $\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(\bigcup _ jA_ j)\le \operatorname {Cap}_ D(\bigcup _ jG_ j)\le \sum _ j\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(A_ j)+\varepsilon $. Finiteness on a compact set $K$ follows from theorem 7.2.5 with $T=1$, applied to $K$ and a compact neighborhood $L$ of $K$ in $D$, since $\| v\| _{L^\infty (L)}\le 1$ for every competitor. Inner regularity of each Radon measure $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n$ (definition 2.2.1 ) gives $\int _ E(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n=\sup _ K\int _ K(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n\le \sup _ K\operatorname {Cap}_ D(K)$ over compact $K\subset E$, and taking the supremum over $v$ gives (1). For (2), $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(E_ j)\le \operatorname {Cap}_ D(E)$ by monotonicity, and for every competitor $v$ monotone convergence gives $\int _ E(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n=\lim _ j\int _{E_ j}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n\le \lim _ j\operatorname {Cap}_ D(E_ j)$; taking the supremum over $v$ gives (2). For (3), choose $a\in D$ and $d>0$ with $D\subset B(a,d)$; the function $|z-a|^2/d^2$ is a competitor, and by ( 7.2.4 ) and proposition 7.2.2 (3) its Monge–Ampère measure is $n!\pi ^{-n}d^{-2n}\, \mathrm dV_{2n}$. Hence (3) holds with $C_ D=\pi ^ nd^{2n}/n!$. For (4), the first inequality holds because the restriction to $B$ of a competitor for $D$ is a competitor for $B$, with the same Monge–Ampère measure on $B$. For the second, write $B=B(a,r)$ and choose $\lambda >0$ such that $\rho =\lambda (|z-a|^2-r^2)<-1$ on a neighborhood of $K$. Given a competitor $v$ for $B$, let $w$ be the function equal to $\max \{ v-1,\rho \} $ on $B$ and to $\rho $ on $D\setminus B$. Since $v-1\le 0$ on $B$ and $\rho =0$ on $\partial B$, proposition 5.9.5 shows that $w$ is plurisubharmonic on $D$. It equals $v-1$ near $K$, satisfies $w\ge -1$ on $D$, and is bounded above by $\Lambda =\max \{ 0,\sup _ D\rho \} $, which does not depend on $v$. Thus $(w+1)/(\Lambda +1)$ is a competitor for $D$, and by locality its Monge–Ampère measure near $K$ is $(\Lambda +1)^{-n}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n$. This gives the second inequality with $C=(\Lambda +1)^ n$; the first inequality holds for all Borel subsets of $B$. For the outer capacities in (4), let $K'$ be a compact neighborhood of $K$ in $B$; the constant obtained for $K'$ also serves for $K$, and we use it. If $A\subset K$ and $G$ is an open subset of $D$ or of $B$ containing $A$, then $G\cap \operatorname{Int}K'$ is open in both $B$ and $D$, contains $A$, lies in $K'$, and has no larger capacity than $G$. Applying the inequalities to these sets and taking infima over $G$ gives them for the outer capacities of $A$. For (5), let $F\colon D\to D'$ be biholomorphic. By proposition 5.9.3 , applied to $F$ and to $F^{-1}$, the map $v\mapsto v\circ F$ is a bijection from the competitors for $D'$ onto the competitors for $D$, and by proposition 7.2.2 (5), $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v\circ F))^ n=F^*\bigl ((\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n\bigr )$. We claim that for every positive Radon measure $\mu $ on $D'$, regarded as a current of bidegree $(n,n)$, the pullback $F^*\mu $ is the image of $\mu $ under $F^{-1}$, that is, $\int \psi \, \mathrm d(F^*\mu )=\int \psi \circ F^{-1}\, \mathrm d\mu $ for every test function $\psi $ on $D$. If $\mu =g\, \mathrm dV_{2n}$ with $g$ smooth, then $F^*\mu =(g\circ F)\, |\det F'|^2\, \mathrm dV_{2n}$, because $F^*(\mathrm dz_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm dz_ n)=\det F'\, \mathrm dz_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm dz_ n$ and similarly for the conjugate forms; since $|\det F'|^2$ is the Jacobian determinant of $F$ as a map of $\mathbb R^{2n}$, the change of variables formula gives the claim. Both sides of the claimed identity are weakly continuous in $\mu $ (proposition 5.6.2 ), and on relatively compact open subsets of $D'$ every $\mu $ is the weak limit of its smooth regularizations, so the claim holds in general. Consequently $(F^*\mu )(F^{-1}(E'))=\mu (E')$ for Borel sets $E'\subset D'$, since two Radon measures that agree on test functions agree on Borel sets (proposition 2.5.3 (4)). Applying this to $\mu =(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n$ and $E'=F(E)$ and taking the supremum over $v$ gives $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(E)=\operatorname {Cap}_{D'}(F(E))$. Since $F$ is a homeomorphism, it maps the open sets containing a set $A$ bijectively onto the open sets containing $F(A)$, so the outer capacities agree as well. $\square$ Proposition 7.4.4 . 815E5BBFC34A Let $D\subset \mathbb C^ n$ be a bounded open set, let $K,L\subset D$ be compact sets with $K\subset \operatorname{Int}L$, and let $V\in \mathrm{PSH}(D)$. There is a constant $C_{K,L}$, depending only on $K$, $L$ and $n$, such that \[  \operatorname {Cap}_ D^*(K\cap \{ V<-s\} ) \le \frac{C_{K,L}}{s}\| V\| _{L^1(L)},\qquad s>0.  \] Moreover, let $E\subset D$ be a set locally contained in pole sets of plurisubharmonic functions, that is, every point of $D$ has an open neighborhood $W\subset D$ and a plurisubharmonic function $V_ W$ on $W$ with $E\cap W\subset \{ V_ W=-\infty \} $. (Such sets are called pluripolar in section 5.47 .) Then $\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(E\cap K)=0$ for every compact set $K\subset D$, and $E$ is contained in a Borel set which has measure zero for every measure $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ n$ with locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions $u_1,\ldots ,u_ n$ on $D$. Proof. Choose an open neighborhood $U$ of $K$ with compact closure in $\operatorname{Int}L$. For every competitor $v$, theorem 7.4.1 , applied to $\overline U\subset \operatorname{Int}L$ with $q=n$ and $u_1=\cdots =u_ n=v$, gives \[  \int _{U\cap \{ V<-s\} }(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n\le s^{-1}\int _{\overline U}|V|\, (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n \le C s^{-1}\| V\| _{L^1(L)}.  \] Since $V$ is upper semicontinuous, $U\cap \{ V<-s\} $ is an open set containing $K\cap \{ V<-s\} $; taking the supremum over $v$ proves the estimate. Since $V$ is locally integrable (theorem 5.9.1 ), $\| V\| _{L^1(L)}<\infty $, and letting $s\to \infty $ gives $\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(K\cap \{ V=-\infty \} )=0$. Now let $E$ be as in the statement. Let $x\in D$, let $W$ and $V_ W$ be as in the hypothesis, and choose $r>0$ with $\overline{B(x,3r)}\subset W$; put $B_ x=B(x,3r)$, $K_ x=\overline{B(x,r)}$ and $L_ x=\overline{B(x,2r)}$. Then $E\cap B_ x\subset \{ V_ W=-\infty \} $, and the restriction of $V_ W$ to $B_ x$ is plurisubharmonic. The estimate just proved, applied in $B_ x$ to this restriction and to $K_ x\subset \operatorname{Int}L_ x$, gives $\operatorname {Cap}^*_{B_ x}(E\cap K_ x)=0$; since every open set in $B_ x$ is open in $D$, the first inequality of proposition 7.4.3 (4) gives $\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(E\cap K_ x)=0$. A compact set $K\subset D$ is covered by finitely many interiors $\operatorname{Int}K_ x$, and subadditivity gives $\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(E\cap K)=0$. Finally, by theorem 7.4.1 , applied on $B_ x$ to $K_ x\subset \operatorname{Int}L_ x$ with $q=n$, the function $V_ W$ is integrable on $K_ x$ for every measure $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ n$ as in the statement, so the Borel set $K_ x\cap \{ V_ W=-\infty \} $ has measure zero for all these measures. Since $D$ has a countable basis, countably many sets $\operatorname{Int}K_ x$ cover $D$, and the union of the corresponding sets $K_ x\cap \{ V_ W=-\infty \} $ is a Borel set with the required property. $\square$ The next estimate controls, uniformly over all competitors, the set where two bounded plurisubharmonic functions with the same boundary values differ. Proposition 7.4.5 (Błocki) . EB80820D2146 Let $B$ be a ball, and let $u$ and $h$ be bounded plurisubharmonic functions on a neighborhood of $\overline B$ with $u\le h$ on $B$ and $u=h$ on a collar of $\partial B$. Let $v$ be a bounded plurisubharmonic function on a neighborhood of $\overline B$, and put $M=\sup _ Bv-\inf _ Bv$. Then \[  \int _ B(h-u)^{n+1}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n \le (n+1)!M^ n\int _ B(h-u)(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^ n.  \] Proof. First suppose that $u$, $h$ and $v$ are smooth; then $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u$, $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h$ and $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v$ are positive $(1,1)$-forms, by proposition 5.9.2 . Subtracting $\sup _ Bv$ from $v$, we may assume $-M\le v\le 0$ on $B$. Put $w=h-u\ge 0$; it vanishes on a collar of $\partial B$. Let $p\ge 2$, and let $R$ be a smooth closed strongly positive form of bidegree $(n-1,n-1)$; the exterior product of $R$ with a positive $(1,1)$-form is then a nonnegative multiple of the volume form, by proposition 5.3.2 , since positive $(1,1)$-forms are strongly positive. Since $\mathrm{d}w\wedge \mathrm{d}^{\mathrm c}w$ is a positive $(1,1)$-form by ( 7.3.1 ) and $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h\wedge R\ge 0$, the chain rule $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(w^ p)=pw^{p-1}\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w+p(p-1)w^{p-2}\mathrm dw\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}w$ gives \[  \begin{aligned}  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(w^ p)\wedge R& =\bigl (p w^{p-1}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h-\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u) +p(p-1)w^{p-2}\mathrm{d}w\wedge \mathrm{d}^{\mathrm c}w\bigr )\wedge R\\ & \ge -pw^{p-1}\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u\wedge R. \end{aligned}  \] Since $w^ p$ has compact support in $B$ and $R$ is closed, ( 7.2.3 ) gives $\int _ Bw^ p\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v\wedge R=(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(vR))(w^ p)=(vR)(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(w^ p))$. As $v\le 0$ and $-v\le M$, the preceding inequality therefore yields \[  \int _ Bw^ p\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v\wedge R =\int _ Bv\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(w^ p)\wedge R \le pM\int _ Bw^{p-1}\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u\wedge R.  \] For $k=1,\ldots ,n$, apply this with $p=n+2-k$ and $R=(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^{n-k}\wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^{k-1}$, a product of positive $(1,1)$-forms, hence strongly positive (proposition 5.3.2 ) and closed. This gives \[  \int _ Bw^{n+2-k}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^{n+1-k}\wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^{k-1}\le (n+2-k)M\int _ Bw^{n+1-k}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^{n-k}\wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^ k,  \] and chaining these $n$ inequalities from $k=1$ to $k=n$ gives the asserted inequality, since $(n+1)n\cdots 2=(n+1)!$. In general, write $B=B(a,r)$ and let $V$ be a collar of $\partial B$ on which $u=h$. Since $\partial B$ is compact, there is $r''<r$ with $\{ z:r''\le |z-a|\le r\} \subset V$; choose $r'\in (r'',r)$ and put $B'=B(a,r')$. Then $h-u$ vanishes on $B\setminus \overline{B(a,r'')}$. Convolve $u$, $h$ and $v$ with the same radial kernel $\rho _\varepsilon $, with $\varepsilon <\min \{ (r'-r'')/2,r-r'\} $ so small that the regularizations are defined, smooth and plurisubharmonic on a neighborhood of $\overline{B'}$ (proposition 5.9.2 ). At points of $\overline{B'}$ they are averages over balls of radius $\varepsilon $ contained in $B$, where $u\le h$; hence $u_\varepsilon \le h_\varepsilon $ on $\overline{B'}$. Moreover $h_\varepsilon -u_\varepsilon $ vanishes on the collar $\{ z:r''+\varepsilon <|z-a|<r-\varepsilon \} $ of $\partial B'$ and outside $\overline{B(a,r''+\varepsilon )}$ in $B'$, hence outside the compact set $\overline{B(a,(r'+r'')/2)}\subset B'$. The values of $v_\varepsilon $ on $B'$ are averages of values of $v$ on $B$, so the oscillation of $v_\varepsilon $ on $B'$ is at most $M$. Apply the smooth case on $B'$ and let $\varepsilon =\varepsilon _ k\downarrow 0$. The weights $(h_\varepsilon -u_\varepsilon )^{n+1}$ and $h_\varepsilon -u_\varepsilon $ are polynomials in decreasing sequences of bounded plurisubharmonic functions, and they, as well as their limits $(h-u)^{n+1}$ and $h-u$, vanish in $B'$ outside the fixed compact set $\overline{B(a,(r'+r'')/2)}$. Testing against a function $\chi \in C^\infty _ c(B')$ equal to $1$ on this set, corollary 7.3.8 lets both sides pass to the limit. Since $h-u$ vanishes on $B\setminus B'$, the limiting inequality on $B'$ is the asserted inequality on $B$. $\square$ In the next two sections we use the proposition through a capacity bound. Let $u$ and $h$ be as in proposition 7.4.5 , and let $D\subset \mathbb C^ n$ be a bounded open set with $\overline B\subset D$. Every competitor $v$ for $\operatorname {Cap}_ D$ has oscillation at most $1$ on $B$. Hence Chebyshev's inequality and the proposition give, for every $\delta >0$, 28751508F174 7.4.6 \begin{equation}  \begin{aligned}  \operatorname {Cap}_ D\bigl (B\cap \{ h-u>\delta \} \bigr ) & \le \sup _ v\frac{1}{\delta ^{n+1}}\int _ B(h-u)^{n+1}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n\\ & \le \frac{(n+1)!}{\delta ^{n+1}}\int _ B(h-u)(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^ n, \end{aligned} \end{equation} where the supremum is taken over all competitors $v$.

title: Theorem 7.4.1
text: Theorem 7.4.1 . 7C68264563C0 Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb C^ n$ be open, $n\ge 1$, let $K,L\subset \Omega $ be compact sets with $K\subset \operatorname{Int}L$, and let $0\le q\le n$ be an integer. There is a constant $C_{K,L,q}$, depending only on $K$, $L$, $n$ and $q$, such that for every $V\in \mathrm{PSH}(\Omega )$ and all locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions $u_1,\ldots ,u_ q$ on $\Omega $, \[  \int _ K |V|\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q\wedge \beta ^{n-q} \le C_{K,L,q}\| V\| _{L^1(L)} \prod _{l=1}^ q\| u_ l\| _{L^\infty (L)}.  \] In particular, the function $V$, with its values $-\infty $ on the pole set $\{ V=-\infty \} $, is locally integrable with respect to the trace measure $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q\wedge \beta ^{n-q}$. Proof. For $q\le n-1$ we integrate $V$ by parts against a cutoff function on a ball, after making the factors coincide near its boundary (Steps 1–4); the case $q=n$ follows by adding one variable (Step 5). Step 1: reductions. By theorem 5.9.1 , $V$ is locally integrable, so $\| V\| _{L^1(L)}<\infty $. For $q=0$ the left-hand side equals $n!\int _ K|V|\, \mathrm{d}V_{2n}\le n!\| V\| _{L^1(L)}$, by ( 5.2.8 ). Let $q\ge 1$. If $\| u_ l\| _{L^\infty (L)}=0$ for some $l$, then $u_ l=0$ on $\operatorname{Int}L$, so the product vanishes on $\operatorname{Int}L\supset K$ by locality. Otherwise we replace each $u_ l$ by $u_ l/(2\| u_ l\| _{L^\infty (L)})-3/2$, which takes values in $[-2,-1]$ on $L$; by proposition 7.2.2 (3) this multiplies the left-hand side by $\prod _ l(2\| u_ l\| _{L^\infty (L)})^{-1}$. For each $a\in K$ choose $R_ a>0$ with $\overline{B(a,R_ a)}\subset \operatorname{Int}L$; finitely many of the balls $B(a,R_ a/2)$ cover $K$, and this choice depends only on $K$ and $L$. Hence it suffices to prove the following: for concentric balls $B'=B(a,R')$ and $B=B(a,R)$ with $R'<R$ and $\overline B\subset \operatorname{Int}L$, there is a constant $C$, depending only on $B'$, $B$, $L$, $n$ and $q$, such that \[  \int _{B'}|V|\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q\wedge \beta ^{n-q}\le C\| V\| _{L^1(L)}  \] whenever $u_1,\ldots ,u_ q$ are plurisubharmonic on $\Omega $ with values in $[-2,-1]$ on $L$. Step 2: a common collar. Put $\psi =|z-a|^2-R^2$ and $b=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi =\beta /\pi $, and choose $\delta >0$ with $\overline{B'}\subset \{ \psi <-\delta \} $. Replace each $u_ l$ by $\max \{ u_ l,A\psi \} $, where $A=2/\delta $; this function is plurisubharmonic on $\Omega $ (proposition 5.9.5 ). By ( 7.3.2 ), with $N=2$ and $U=\operatorname{Int}L$, it is unchanged on $\{ \psi <-\delta \} $, it equals $A\psi $ on the collar $V_0=\{ z\in \operatorname{Int}L:\psi (z)>-\delta /2\} $ of $\partial B$, and it takes values in $[-2,0)$ on $B$. Let $S=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q$ be the product of the modified functions. Put $\tau =\delta /4$ and $B_\tau =\{ \psi <-\tau \} $. Then $\overline{B'}\subset B_\tau $, and on the neighborhood $V_0$ of $\overline B\setminus B_\tau $ we have $S=(A\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi )^ q=A^ qb^ q$ by proposition 7.2.2 (1),(2). By lemma 2.5.1 (4) there is $\theta \in C^\infty _ c(B)$ with $0\le \theta \le 1$ and $\theta =1$ on a neighborhood of $\overline{B_\tau }$; the function $\chi =-\psi \theta $ is smooth, nonnegative, has compact support in $B$, and equals $-\psi $ on a neighborhood of $\overline{B_\tau }$. All these choices depend only on $B'$, $B$ and $L$. Step 3: smooth $V$ and $q\le n-1$. Suppose that $q\le n-1$ and that $V$ is smooth and plurisubharmonic on a neighborhood of $\overline B$ with $V\le 0$ on $B_\tau $. The signed measure $S\wedge b^{n-q-1}\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi $ has compact support in $B$. Splitting its integral against $V$ over $B_\tau $, where $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi =-b$, and over $B\setminus B_\tau \subset V_0$, where $S=A^ qb^ q$, we obtain \[  \begin{aligned}  \int _{B_\tau }(-V)S\wedge b^{n-q} & =\int _ B V S\wedge b^{n-q-1}\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi -A^ q\int _{B\setminus B_\tau }V b^{n-1}\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi \\ & =\int _ B\chi \, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}V\wedge S\wedge b^{n-q-1} -A^ q\int _{B\setminus B_\tau }V b^{n-1}\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi . \end{aligned}  \] The second equality holds because the first integral is $(VS\wedge b^{n-q-1})(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi )=\bigl (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(VS\wedge b^{n-q-1})\bigr )(\chi )$, and $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(VS\wedge b^{n-q-1})=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}V\wedge S\wedge b^{n-q-1}$ by ( 7.2.3 ), the current $S\wedge b^{n-q-1}$ being closed. The smooth form $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}V$ is closed, and it is strongly positive, since its coefficient matrix is positive semidefinite (proposition 5.9.2 ) and weak and strong positivity agree in bidegree $(1,1)$ (section 5.3 ); so by proposition 7.2.2 (4), with $T=1$ and $\gamma =\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}V$, the current $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}V\wedge S$ is the product $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}V$ with the closed positive base current $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}V$ of bidimension $(n-1,n-1)$. Choose a compact set $L'\subset B$ whose interior contains $\operatorname{Supp}\chi $. The first term is at most $\pi ^{q+1-n}\sup \chi $ times the mass of the trace measure of $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}V$ on $\operatorname{Supp}\chi $. Since the modified $u_ l$ take values in $[-2,0)$ on $B$, theorem 7.2.5 , applied to $\operatorname{Supp}\chi \subset \operatorname{Int}L'$, shows that the first term is at most $C\| \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}V\| _{L'}$, with $C$ depending only on $\chi $, $L'$, $n$ and $q$. Let $\chi '\in C^\infty _ c(B)$ satisfy $0\le \chi '\le 1$ and $\chi '=1$ on $L'$. Since $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}V\wedge \beta ^{n-1}\ge 0$, \[  \| \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}V\| _{L'}\le \int \chi '\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}V\wedge \frac{\beta ^{n-1}}{(n-1)!}=\int V\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi '\wedge \frac{\beta ^{n-1}}{(n-1)!}\le C\int _ B|V|\, \mathrm{d}V_{2n},  \] where $C$ bounds the coefficient of the smooth $(n,n)$-form $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi '\wedge \beta ^{n-1}/(n-1)!$. The collar term is bounded by the same quantity, because $b^{n-1}\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\chi $ has bounded smooth coefficients. Hence \[  \int _{B_\tau }(-V)S\wedge b^{n-q}\le C\int _ B|V|\, \mathrm{d}V_{2n}.  \] Step 4: general $V$ and $q\le n-1$. Let $V\in \mathrm{PSH}(\Omega )$, and choose $r_0>0$ with $2r_0<\operatorname {dist}(\overline B,\mathbb C^ n\setminus \operatorname{Int}L)$. The function $V$ is subharmonic (theorem 5.9.1 ). If $x$ lies within distance $r_0$ of $\overline B$, then $\overline{B(x,r_0)}\subset \operatorname{Int}L$, and the ball submean inequality of theorem 3.4.5 (2) gives \[  V(x)\le \frac1{|B(x,r_0)|}\int _{B(x,r_0)}V\, \mathrm dV_{2n}\le c_0\| V\| _{L^1(L)},\qquad c_0=|B(0,r_0)|^{-1};  \] put $c=c_0\| V\| _{L^1(L)}$. For $0<\varepsilon <r_0$ the regularization $V_\varepsilon =V*\rho _\varepsilon $ is smooth and plurisubharmonic on the neighborhood $\{ z:\operatorname {dist}(z,\overline B)<r_0\} $ of $\overline B$ (proposition 5.9.2 ), since this neighborhood lies in $\Omega _\varepsilon $. It satisfies $V_\varepsilon \le c$ on $\overline B$, since $V_\varepsilon (x)$ is an average of values of $V$ at points within distance $\varepsilon $ of $x$, and $\int _ B|V_\varepsilon |\, \mathrm{d}V_{2n}\le \int \rho _\varepsilon (y)\int _ B|V(x-y)|\, \mathrm dV_{2n}(x)\, \mathrm dV_{2n}(y)\le \| V\| _{L^1(L)}$ by Tonelli's theorem, since $B-y\subset L$ for $|y|\le \varepsilon $. Applying Step 3 to $V_\varepsilon -c$ gives \[  \int _{B_\tau }(c-V_\varepsilon )\, S\wedge b^{n-q}\le C\bigl (\| V\| _{L^1(L)}+c|B|\bigr )\le C'\| V\| _{L^1(L)}.  \] As $\varepsilon \downarrow 0$, the nonnegative functions $c-V_\varepsilon $ increase to $c-V$, by ( 3.4.13 ), so monotone convergence gives the same bound for $\int _{B_\tau }(c-V)\, S\wedge b^{n-q}$. Since $V\le c$ on $B_\tau $, we have $|V|\le (c-V)+c$ there, and the mass of $S\wedge b^{n-q}$ on $B_\tau $ is bounded by a constant depending only on $B'$, $B$, $n$ and $q$, by theorem 7.2.5 applied to $\overline{B_\tau }\subset B=\operatorname{Int}\overline B$, since the modified $u_ l$ take values in $[-2,0]$ on $\overline B$. Since $S$ coincides with the original product on $B'\subset B_\tau $, by locality, this proves the estimate of Step 1 for $q\le n-1$. By the finite cover and the normalizations of Step 1, the theorem holds for $q\le n-1$, in every dimension. Step 5: the case $q=n$. Consider $\mathbb C^{n+1}$ with coordinates $(z,w)$, the unit disc $\Delta \subset \mathbb C$, and the projection $p(z,w)=z$; let $\beta _ z$, $\beta _ w$ be the forms ( 5.2.8 ) in the variables $z$ and $w$, so that $\beta _ z+\beta _ w$ is the form $\beta $ of $\mathbb C^{n+1}$, and $\beta _ w=\mathrm dV_2(w)$. By proposition 5.9.3 , the functions $u_ l\circ p$ are locally bounded and plurisubharmonic on $\Omega \times \Delta $, and $V\circ p$ is plurisubharmonic there, since it is not identically $-\infty $ on any connected component $\Omega _0\times \Delta $ of $\Omega \times \Delta $. Let $\mu =\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ n$, a positive measure on $\Omega $. We claim that \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u_1\circ p)\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u_ n\circ p)\wedge (\beta _ z+\beta _ w)=\mu \otimes \mathrm{d}V_2.  \] If the $u_ l$ are smooth, then $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u_ l\circ p)=p^*\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ l$, so the product of these $n$ factors is the pullback $p^*\mu $ of the $(n,n)$-form $\mu =g\, \mathrm dV_{2n}$ (proposition 7.2.2 (1)). Its exterior product with $\beta _ z$ is $p^*(\mu \wedge \beta )=0$, since $\mu \wedge \beta $ has bidegree $(n+1,n+1)$ on $\mathbb C^ n$, and its exterior product with $\beta _ w$ is $g(z)\, \mathrm dV_{2n}(z)\wedge \mathrm dV_2(w)$, the density of $\mu \otimes \mathrm dV_2$. In general, let $u_{l,\varepsilon }=u_ l*\rho _\varepsilon $, which are smooth plurisubharmonic functions on $\Omega _{\varepsilon _0}$ for $\varepsilon <\varepsilon _0$, decreasing to $u_ l$ as $\varepsilon \downarrow 0$ (proposition 5.9.2 ). By theorem 7.3.7 , applied on $\Omega _{\varepsilon _0}\times \Delta $ to the functions $u_{l,\varepsilon }\circ p$, which decrease to $u_ l\circ p$, the left-hand sides for $u_{l,\varepsilon }$ converge weakly to the left-hand side for $u_ l$. By the same theorem on $\Omega _{\varepsilon _0}$, the measures $\mu _\varepsilon =\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{1,\varepsilon }\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{n,\varepsilon }$ converge weakly to $\mu $; hence $\mu _\varepsilon \otimes \mathrm dV_2\to \mu \otimes \mathrm dV_2$, because for a test function $\varphi $ on $\Omega _{\varepsilon _0}\times \Delta $ we have $\int \varphi \, \mathrm d(\mu _\varepsilon \otimes \mathrm dV_2)=\int \Phi \, \mathrm d\mu _\varepsilon $ with $\Phi (z)=\int _\Delta \varphi (z,w)\, \mathrm dV_2(w)$, a test function on $\Omega _{\varepsilon _0}$ (differentiate under the integral sign). Since $\varepsilon _0$ is arbitrary, the claim follows from the smooth case. Now apply the case already proved in dimension $n+1$, with $q=n\le (n+1)-1$, to the compact sets $\widetilde K=K\times \{ |w|\le 1/2\} $ and $\widetilde L=L\times \{ |w|\le 3/4\} $ in $\Omega \times \Delta $; note that $\widetilde K\subset \operatorname{Int}\widetilde L$. By the claim and Fubini's theorem, the left-hand side of the estimate for $V\circ p$ and the $u_ l\circ p$ is $\frac\pi 4\int _ K|V|\, \mathrm d\mu $, while $\| V\circ p\| _{L^1(\widetilde L)}=\frac{9\pi }{16}\| V\| _{L^1(L)}$ and $\| u_ l\circ p\| _{L^\infty (\widetilde L)}=\| u_ l\| _{L^\infty (L)}$. Hence the estimate holds in $\mathbb C^ n$ with the constant $\frac94C_{\widetilde K,\widetilde L,n}$, which depends only on $K$, $L$ and $n$. This proves the case $q=n$. $\square$

title: Definition 7.4.2
text: Definition 7.4.2 . E9E7C75396D2 Let $D\subset \mathbb {C}^ n$, $n\ge 1$, be a bounded open set. The Monge–Ampère capacity of a Borel set $E\subset D$ is \[  \operatorname {Cap}_ D(E)=\sup \left\{ \int _ E(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n: v\in \mathrm{PSH}(D),\  0\le v\le 1\right\} .  \] The functions $v$ in this supremum are called competitors for $\operatorname {Cap}_ D$. The outer capacity of an arbitrary set $A\subset D$ is \[  \operatorname {Cap}_ D^*(A)=\inf \{ \operatorname {Cap}_ D(G):A\subset G\subset D, \  G\text{ open}\} .  \]

title: Proposition 7.4.3
text: Proposition 7.4.3 . 97EFDB6FDEE3 Let $D\subset \mathbb C^ n$ be a bounded open set. The set functions $\operatorname {Cap}_ D$ and $\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D$ are increasing with respect to inclusion and countably subadditive. Moreover: $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(K)<\infty $ for every compact $K\subset D$, and $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(E)=\sup \{ \operatorname {Cap}_ D(K):K\subset E\text{ compact}\} $ for every Borel set $E\subset D$; if $E_ j\subset D$ are Borel sets increasing to $E$, then $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(E_ j)\to \operatorname {Cap}_ D(E)$; there is a constant $C_ D$ such that $|E|\le C_ D\operatorname {Cap}_ D(E)$ for every Borel set $E\subset D$, where $|E|$ is Lebesgue measure; if $B\Subset D$ is a ball and $K\subset B$ is compact, there is a constant $C$ such that, for every Borel set $E\subset K$, \[  \operatorname {Cap}_ D(E)\le \operatorname {Cap}_ B(E) \le C\operatorname {Cap}_ D(E),  \] and the same inequalities hold for the outer capacities of arbitrary subsets of $K$; both capacities are invariant under biholomorphisms between bounded open sets: if $F\colon D\to D'$ is biholomorphic, then $\operatorname {Cap}_{D'}(F(E))=\operatorname {Cap}_ D(E)$ for Borel sets $E\subset D$ and $\operatorname {Cap}^*_{D'}(F(A))=\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(A)$ for arbitrary sets $A\subset D$. Proof. For each competitor $v$, the measure $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n$ is increasing and countably subadditive on Borel sets: $\int _{\bigcup _ jE_ j}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n\le \sum _ j\int _{E_ j}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n\le \sum _ j\operatorname {Cap}_ D(E_ j)$. Taking the supremum over $v$ gives the same properties for $\operatorname {Cap}_ D$. Outer capacity is increasing by definition. For countable subadditivity, given sets $A_ j$ with $\sum _ j\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(A_ j)<\infty $ and $\varepsilon >0$, choose open sets $G_ j\supset A_ j$ with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G_ j)<\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(A_ j)+\varepsilon 2^{-j}$; then $\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(\bigcup _ jA_ j)\le \operatorname {Cap}_ D(\bigcup _ jG_ j)\le \sum _ j\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(A_ j)+\varepsilon $. Finiteness on a compact set $K$ follows from theorem 7.2.5 with $T=1$, applied to $K$ and a compact neighborhood $L$ of $K$ in $D$, since $\| v\| _{L^\infty (L)}\le 1$ for every competitor. Inner regularity of each Radon measure $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n$ (definition 2.2.1 ) gives $\int _ E(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n=\sup _ K\int _ K(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n\le \sup _ K\operatorname {Cap}_ D(K)$ over compact $K\subset E$, and taking the supremum over $v$ gives (1). For (2), $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(E_ j)\le \operatorname {Cap}_ D(E)$ by monotonicity, and for every competitor $v$ monotone convergence gives $\int _ E(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n=\lim _ j\int _{E_ j}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n\le \lim _ j\operatorname {Cap}_ D(E_ j)$; taking the supremum over $v$ gives (2). For (3), choose $a\in D$ and $d>0$ with $D\subset B(a,d)$; the function $|z-a|^2/d^2$ is a competitor, and by ( 7.2.4 ) and proposition 7.2.2 (3) its Monge–Ampère measure is $n!\pi ^{-n}d^{-2n}\, \mathrm dV_{2n}$. Hence (3) holds with $C_ D=\pi ^ nd^{2n}/n!$. For (4), the first inequality holds because the restriction to $B$ of a competitor for $D$ is a competitor for $B$, with the same Monge–Ampère measure on $B$. For the second, write $B=B(a,r)$ and choose $\lambda >0$ such that $\rho =\lambda (|z-a|^2-r^2)<-1$ on a neighborhood of $K$. Given a competitor $v$ for $B$, let $w$ be the function equal to $\max \{ v-1,\rho \} $ on $B$ and to $\rho $ on $D\setminus B$. Since $v-1\le 0$ on $B$ and $\rho =0$ on $\partial B$, proposition 5.9.5 shows that $w$ is plurisubharmonic on $D$. It equals $v-1$ near $K$, satisfies $w\ge -1$ on $D$, and is bounded above by $\Lambda =\max \{ 0,\sup _ D\rho \} $, which does not depend on $v$. Thus $(w+1)/(\Lambda +1)$ is a competitor for $D$, and by locality its Monge–Ampère measure near $K$ is $(\Lambda +1)^{-n}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n$. This gives the second inequality with $C=(\Lambda +1)^ n$; the first inequality holds for all Borel subsets of $B$. For the outer capacities in (4), let $K'$ be a compact neighborhood of $K$ in $B$; the constant obtained for $K'$ also serves for $K$, and we use it. If $A\subset K$ and $G$ is an open subset of $D$ or of $B$ containing $A$, then $G\cap \operatorname{Int}K'$ is open in both $B$ and $D$, contains $A$, lies in $K'$, and has no larger capacity than $G$. Applying the inequalities to these sets and taking infima over $G$ gives them for the outer capacities of $A$. For (5), let $F\colon D\to D'$ be biholomorphic. By proposition 5.9.3 , applied to $F$ and to $F^{-1}$, the map $v\mapsto v\circ F$ is a bijection from the competitors for $D'$ onto the competitors for $D$, and by proposition 7.2.2 (5), $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v\circ F))^ n=F^*\bigl ((\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n\bigr )$. We claim that for every positive Radon measure $\mu $ on $D'$, regarded as a current of bidegree $(n,n)$, the pullback $F^*\mu $ is the image of $\mu $ under $F^{-1}$, that is, $\int \psi \, \mathrm d(F^*\mu )=\int \psi \circ F^{-1}\, \mathrm d\mu $ for every test function $\psi $ on $D$. If $\mu =g\, \mathrm dV_{2n}$ with $g$ smooth, then $F^*\mu =(g\circ F)\, |\det F'|^2\, \mathrm dV_{2n}$, because $F^*(\mathrm dz_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm dz_ n)=\det F'\, \mathrm dz_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm dz_ n$ and similarly for the conjugate forms; since $|\det F'|^2$ is the Jacobian determinant of $F$ as a map of $\mathbb R^{2n}$, the change of variables formula gives the claim. Both sides of the claimed identity are weakly continuous in $\mu $ (proposition 5.6.2 ), and on relatively compact open subsets of $D'$ every $\mu $ is the weak limit of its smooth regularizations, so the claim holds in general. Consequently $(F^*\mu )(F^{-1}(E'))=\mu (E')$ for Borel sets $E'\subset D'$, since two Radon measures that agree on test functions agree on Borel sets (proposition 2.5.3 (4)). Applying this to $\mu =(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n$ and $E'=F(E)$ and taking the supremum over $v$ gives $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(E)=\operatorname {Cap}_{D'}(F(E))$. Since $F$ is a homeomorphism, it maps the open sets containing a set $A$ bijectively onto the open sets containing $F(A)$, so the outer capacities agree as well. $\square$

title: Proposition 7.4.4
text: Proposition 7.4.4 . 815E5BBFC34A Let $D\subset \mathbb C^ n$ be a bounded open set, let $K,L\subset D$ be compact sets with $K\subset \operatorname{Int}L$, and let $V\in \mathrm{PSH}(D)$. There is a constant $C_{K,L}$, depending only on $K$, $L$ and $n$, such that \[  \operatorname {Cap}_ D^*(K\cap \{ V<-s\} ) \le \frac{C_{K,L}}{s}\| V\| _{L^1(L)},\qquad s>0.  \] Moreover, let $E\subset D$ be a set locally contained in pole sets of plurisubharmonic functions, that is, every point of $D$ has an open neighborhood $W\subset D$ and a plurisubharmonic function $V_ W$ on $W$ with $E\cap W\subset \{ V_ W=-\infty \} $. (Such sets are called pluripolar in section 5.47 .) Then $\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(E\cap K)=0$ for every compact set $K\subset D$, and $E$ is contained in a Borel set which has measure zero for every measure $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ n$ with locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions $u_1,\ldots ,u_ n$ on $D$. Proof. Choose an open neighborhood $U$ of $K$ with compact closure in $\operatorname{Int}L$. For every competitor $v$, theorem 7.4.1 , applied to $\overline U\subset \operatorname{Int}L$ with $q=n$ and $u_1=\cdots =u_ n=v$, gives \[  \int _{U\cap \{ V<-s\} }(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n\le s^{-1}\int _{\overline U}|V|\, (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n \le C s^{-1}\| V\| _{L^1(L)}.  \] Since $V$ is upper semicontinuous, $U\cap \{ V<-s\} $ is an open set containing $K\cap \{ V<-s\} $; taking the supremum over $v$ proves the estimate. Since $V$ is locally integrable (theorem 5.9.1 ), $\| V\| _{L^1(L)}<\infty $, and letting $s\to \infty $ gives $\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(K\cap \{ V=-\infty \} )=0$. Now let $E$ be as in the statement. Let $x\in D$, let $W$ and $V_ W$ be as in the hypothesis, and choose $r>0$ with $\overline{B(x,3r)}\subset W$; put $B_ x=B(x,3r)$, $K_ x=\overline{B(x,r)}$ and $L_ x=\overline{B(x,2r)}$. Then $E\cap B_ x\subset \{ V_ W=-\infty \} $, and the restriction of $V_ W$ to $B_ x$ is plurisubharmonic. The estimate just proved, applied in $B_ x$ to this restriction and to $K_ x\subset \operatorname{Int}L_ x$, gives $\operatorname {Cap}^*_{B_ x}(E\cap K_ x)=0$; since every open set in $B_ x$ is open in $D$, the first inequality of proposition 7.4.3 (4) gives $\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(E\cap K_ x)=0$. A compact set $K\subset D$ is covered by finitely many interiors $\operatorname{Int}K_ x$, and subadditivity gives $\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(E\cap K)=0$. Finally, by theorem 7.4.1 , applied on $B_ x$ to $K_ x\subset \operatorname{Int}L_ x$ with $q=n$, the function $V_ W$ is integrable on $K_ x$ for every measure $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ n$ as in the statement, so the Borel set $K_ x\cap \{ V_ W=-\infty \} $ has measure zero for all these measures. Since $D$ has a countable basis, countably many sets $\operatorname{Int}K_ x$ cover $D$, and the union of the corresponding sets $K_ x\cap \{ V_ W=-\infty \} $ is a Borel set with the required property. $\square$

title: Proposition 7.4.5 (Błocki)
text: Proposition 7.4.5 (Błocki) . EB80820D2146 Let $B$ be a ball, and let $u$ and $h$ be bounded plurisubharmonic functions on a neighborhood of $\overline B$ with $u\le h$ on $B$ and $u=h$ on a collar of $\partial B$. Let $v$ be a bounded plurisubharmonic function on a neighborhood of $\overline B$, and put $M=\sup _ Bv-\inf _ Bv$. Then \[  \int _ B(h-u)^{n+1}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n \le (n+1)!M^ n\int _ B(h-u)(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^ n.  \] Proof. First suppose that $u$, $h$ and $v$ are smooth; then $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u$, $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h$ and $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v$ are positive $(1,1)$-forms, by proposition 5.9.2 . Subtracting $\sup _ Bv$ from $v$, we may assume $-M\le v\le 0$ on $B$. Put $w=h-u\ge 0$; it vanishes on a collar of $\partial B$. Let $p\ge 2$, and let $R$ be a smooth closed strongly positive form of bidegree $(n-1,n-1)$; the exterior product of $R$ with a positive $(1,1)$-form is then a nonnegative multiple of the volume form, by proposition 5.3.2 , since positive $(1,1)$-forms are strongly positive. Since $\mathrm{d}w\wedge \mathrm{d}^{\mathrm c}w$ is a positive $(1,1)$-form by ( 7.3.1 ) and $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h\wedge R\ge 0$, the chain rule $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(w^ p)=pw^{p-1}\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w+p(p-1)w^{p-2}\mathrm dw\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}w$ gives \[  \begin{aligned}  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(w^ p)\wedge R& =\bigl (p w^{p-1}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h-\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u) +p(p-1)w^{p-2}\mathrm{d}w\wedge \mathrm{d}^{\mathrm c}w\bigr )\wedge R\\ & \ge -pw^{p-1}\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u\wedge R. \end{aligned}  \] Since $w^ p$ has compact support in $B$ and $R$ is closed, ( 7.2.3 ) gives $\int _ Bw^ p\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v\wedge R=(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(vR))(w^ p)=(vR)(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(w^ p))$. As $v\le 0$ and $-v\le M$, the preceding inequality therefore yields \[  \int _ Bw^ p\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v\wedge R =\int _ Bv\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(w^ p)\wedge R \le pM\int _ Bw^{p-1}\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u\wedge R.  \] For $k=1,\ldots ,n$, apply this with $p=n+2-k$ and $R=(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^{n-k}\wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^{k-1}$, a product of positive $(1,1)$-forms, hence strongly positive (proposition 5.3.2 ) and closed. This gives \[  \int _ Bw^{n+2-k}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^{n+1-k}\wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^{k-1}\le (n+2-k)M\int _ Bw^{n+1-k}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^{n-k}\wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^ k,  \] and chaining these $n$ inequalities from $k=1$ to $k=n$ gives the asserted inequality, since $(n+1)n\cdots 2=(n+1)!$. In general, write $B=B(a,r)$ and let $V$ be a collar of $\partial B$ on which $u=h$. Since $\partial B$ is compact, there is $r''<r$ with $\{ z:r''\le |z-a|\le r\} \subset V$; choose $r'\in (r'',r)$ and put $B'=B(a,r')$. Then $h-u$ vanishes on $B\setminus \overline{B(a,r'')}$. Convolve $u$, $h$ and $v$ with the same radial kernel $\rho _\varepsilon $, with $\varepsilon <\min \{ (r'-r'')/2,r-r'\} $ so small that the regularizations are defined, smooth and plurisubharmonic on a neighborhood of $\overline{B'}$ (proposition 5.9.2 ). At points of $\overline{B'}$ they are averages over balls of radius $\varepsilon $ contained in $B$, where $u\le h$; hence $u_\varepsilon \le h_\varepsilon $ on $\overline{B'}$. Moreover $h_\varepsilon -u_\varepsilon $ vanishes on the collar $\{ z:r''+\varepsilon <|z-a|<r-\varepsilon \} $ of $\partial B'$ and outside $\overline{B(a,r''+\varepsilon )}$ in $B'$, hence outside the compact set $\overline{B(a,(r'+r'')/2)}\subset B'$. The values of $v_\varepsilon $ on $B'$ are averages of values of $v$ on $B$, so the oscillation of $v_\varepsilon $ on $B'$ is at most $M$. Apply the smooth case on $B'$ and let $\varepsilon =\varepsilon _ k\downarrow 0$. The weights $(h_\varepsilon -u_\varepsilon )^{n+1}$ and $h_\varepsilon -u_\varepsilon $ are polynomials in decreasing sequences of bounded plurisubharmonic functions, and they, as well as their limits $(h-u)^{n+1}$ and $h-u$, vanish in $B'$ outside the fixed compact set $\overline{B(a,(r'+r'')/2)}$. Testing against a function $\chi \in C^\infty _ c(B')$ equal to $1$ on this set, corollary 7.3.8 lets both sides pass to the limit. Since $h-u$ vanishes on $B\setminus B'$, the limiting inequality on $B'$ is the asserted inequality on $B$. $\square$

title: Equation 7.4.6
text: 28751508F174 7.4.6 \begin{equation}  \begin{aligned}  \operatorname {Cap}_ D\bigl (B\cap \{ h-u>\delta \} \bigr ) & \le \sup _ v\frac{1}{\delta ^{n+1}}\int _ B(h-u)^{n+1}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n\\ & \le \frac{(n+1)!}{\delta ^{n+1}}\int _ B(h-u)(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^ n, \end{aligned} \end{equation}

title: 7.5 Quasi-continuity and convergence in capacity
text: Throughout this section and the next, $D\subset \mathbb {C}^ n$, $n\ge 1$, is a bounded open set. By theorem 4.1.30 , locally integrable subharmonic functions are quasi-continuous in the sense of 1: they are continuous outside open sets of arbitrarily small relative capacity. We now define quasi-continuity with respect to the Monge–Ampère capacity instead, which is the meaning of the term in the following constructions, prove that plurisubharmonic functions are quasi-continuous in this sense, and then show that the products are continuous under convergence in capacity. Definition 7.5.1 . A2CACA24130B A Borel function $f\colon D\to [-\infty ,\infty ]$ is quasi-continuous (for $\operatorname {Cap}_ D$) if for every compact set $K\subset D$ and every $\varepsilon >0$ there is an open set $G\subset D$ with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G)<\varepsilon $ such that the restriction of $f$ to $K\setminus G$ is continuous. Here $[-\infty ,\infty ]$ carries its order topology. The same definition applies to a function defined on an open subset $W\subset D$, with compact sets $K\subset W$ and still with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D$. The sum $f_1+f_2$ and the difference $f_1-f_2$ of two real-valued quasi-continuous functions $f_1,f_2$ are quasi-continuous, and so is $\Phi \circ f_1$ for every continuous function $\Phi \colon \mathbb R\to \mathbb R$. Indeed, these functions are Borel. Given $K$ and $\varepsilon $, choose open sets $G_ i\subset D$ with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G_ i)<\varepsilon /2$ such that $f_ i$ is continuous on $K\setminus G_ i$, $i=1,2$. Then $G=G_1\cup G_2$ satisfies $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G)<\varepsilon $ by subadditivity (proposition 7.4.3 ), and $f_1+f_2$ and $f_1-f_2$ are continuous on $K\setminus G$, as sums and differences of continuous real functions there; similarly, $\Phi \circ f_1$ is continuous on $K\setminus G_1$. Theorem 7.5.2 . C39FEC1AB985 Let $u\in \mathrm{PSH}(D)$. For every $\varepsilon >0$ there is an open set $G\subset D$ with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G)<\varepsilon $ which contains the pole set $\{ u=-\infty \} $ and such that the restriction of $u$ to $D\setminus G$ is finite and continuous. In particular $u$ is quasi-continuous. Proof. Step 1: locally bounded $u$. Let $u$ be locally bounded, $K\subset D$ compact and $\varepsilon >0$; we find an open set $G\subset D$ with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G)<\varepsilon $ such that $u$ is continuous on $K\setminus G$. For each $x\in K$ choose $r_ x>0$ with $\overline{B(x,3r_ x)}\subset D$; finitely many balls $B(x_ i,r_{x_ i})$, $1\le i\le m$, cover $K$. Suppose that for each $i$ we find an open set $G_ i$ with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G_ i)<\varepsilon /m$ such that $u$ is continuous on $\overline{B(x_ i,r_{x_ i})}\setminus G_ i$. Then $G=\bigcup _ iG_ i$ satisfies $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G)<\varepsilon $, and $u$ is continuous on $K\setminus G$, because the finitely many sets $(K\setminus G)\cap \overline{B(x_ i,r_{x_ i})}$ are closed in $K\setminus G$ and cover it, and $u$ is continuous on each of them. We may therefore assume that $K=\overline{B'}$, where $B'=B(x,r)$, $B=B(x,2r)$ and $B_1=B(x,3r)$ satisfy $\overline{B_1}\subset D$. Subtracting a constant, we may assume that $-N\le u\le -1$ on $B_1$. Let $j>2/r$. Since $U=B(x,5r/2)$, a neighborhood of $\overline B$, lies at distance $r/2>1/j$ from $\mathbb C^ n\setminus B_1$, the regularization $u*\rho _{1/j}$ is smooth and plurisubharmonic on $U$ and takes values in $[-N,-1]$ there; moreover, $u*\rho _{1/j}$ decreases to $u$ as $j\to \infty $ (proposition 5.9.2 ). Put $\psi =|z-x|^2-4r^2$, choose $\delta >0$ with $\overline{B'}\subset \{ \psi <-\delta \} $, and let $g=\max \{ u,A\psi \} $ and $g_ j=\max \{ u*\rho _{1/j},A\psi \} $, with $A=N/\delta $, be the functions ( 7.3.2 ) on $U$. The $g_ j$ are continuous and plurisubharmonic on $U$ and decrease to $g$; moreover, $g=u$ on $\{ \psi <-\delta \} \supset \overline{B'}$, and $g_ j=g=A\psi $ on a collar of $\partial B$. For $\delta '>0$ put $G_{j,\delta '}=\{ z\in B:g_ j(z)-g(z)>\delta '\} $; it is open, because $g_ j$ is continuous and $g$ is upper semicontinuous. By ( 7.4.6 ), applied with $h=g_ j$, $u=g$ and $\delta '$ in place of $\delta $, \[  \operatorname {Cap}_ D(G_{j,\delta '})\le \frac{(n+1)!}{\delta '^{n+1}}\int _ B(g_ j-g)(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g)^ n.  \] The right-hand side tends to zero as $j\to \infty $ by dominated convergence: $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g)^ n$ has finite mass on $B$, since $g$ is bounded and plurisubharmonic near $\overline B$, and the functions $g_ j-g\ge 0$ are bounded on $B$ uniformly in $j$ and decrease to zero. Choose $j_1<j_2<\cdots $ such that $G_ l=G_{j_ l,2^{-l}}$ satisfies $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G_ l)<\varepsilon 2^{-l}$, and let $G=\bigcup _ lG_ l$. Then $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G)<\varepsilon $, and on $B\setminus G$ we have $0\le g_{j_ l}-g\le 2^{-l}$ for every $l$. Thus $g$ is a uniform limit of continuous functions on $B\setminus G$, hence continuous there; in particular $u=g$ is continuous on $\overline{B'}\setminus G$. Step 2: arbitrary $u$. Let $K\subset D$ be compact and $\varepsilon >0$. By proposition 7.4.4 , applied to $K$ and a compact neighborhood $L$ of $K$ in $D$, there is $s>0$ with $\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(K\cap \{ u<-s\} )<\varepsilon /2$, and hence an open set $G_1\supset K\cap \{ u<-s\} $ with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G_1)<\varepsilon /2$. By Step 1, applied to the locally bounded plurisubharmonic function $\max \{ u,-s\} $, there is an open set $G_2$ with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G_2)<\varepsilon /2$ such that $\max \{ u,-s\} $ is continuous on $K\setminus G_2$. On $K\setminus (G_1\cup G_2)$ we have $u\ge -s$, hence $u=\max \{ u,-s\} $. Thus $G=G_1\cup G_2$ contains $K\cap \{ u=-\infty \} $, $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G)<\varepsilon $, and $u$ is finite and continuous on $K\setminus G$. Step 3: a single exceptional set. Choose compact sets $K_ l$ with $K_ l\subset \operatorname{Int}K_{l+1}$ and $\bigcup _ lK_ l=D$. By Step 2 there are open sets $G^{(l)}\supset K_ l\cap \{ u=-\infty \} $ with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G^{(l)})<\varepsilon 2^{-l}$ such that $u$ is finite and continuous on $K_ l\setminus G^{(l)}$. Put $G=\bigcup _ lG^{(l)}$. Then $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G)<\varepsilon $, and $G$ contains the pole set of $u$. Every $x\in D\setminus G$ lies in some $\operatorname{Int}K_ l$, and on the neighborhood $\operatorname{Int}K_ l\setminus G$ of $x$ in $D\setminus G$ the function $u$ is a restriction of the continuous function $u|_{K_ l\setminus G^{(l)}}$. Hence $u|_{D\setminus G}$ is finite and continuous. $\square$ In the proofs below we extend continuous functions from compact sets, using the following elementary case of Tietze's extension theorem. Lemma 7.5.3 . D127F8356D96 Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space, let $F\subset X$ be compact, and let $f\colon F\to \mathbb R$ be continuous with $|f|\le a$. Then $f$ has a continuous extension $g\colon X\to \mathbb R$ with $|g|\le a$. Proof. If $F=\varnothing $ or $a=0$, take $g=0$. Otherwise, for $L>0$ put \[  f_ L(x)=\max \Bigl \{ -a,\min \bigl \{ a,\inf _{y\in F}(f(y)+L\, d(x,y))\bigr \} \Bigr \} ,\qquad x\in X.  \] The infimum is finite, since $f\ge -a$, and as an infimum of functions that are Lipschitz with constant $L$ it is Lipschitz with constant $L$; hence $f_ L$ is continuous and $|f_ L|\le a$. We claim that $f_ L\to f$ uniformly on $F$ as $L\to \infty $. Taking $y=x$ shows $f_ L\le f$ on $F$. Given $\eta >0$, uniform continuity of $f$ on the compact set $F$ gives $r>0$ with $|f(y)-f(x)|<\eta $ for $x,y\in F$ with $d(x,y)<r$. Let $Lr>2a$ and $x\in F$. Points $y\in F$ with $d(x,y)\ge r$ give $f(y)+L\, d(x,y)\ge -a+Lr>a\ge f(x)$, and the other points give $f(y)+L\, d(x,y)>f(x)-\eta $. Hence the infimum is at least $f(x)-\eta $, and so is $f_ L(x)$, because $a\ge f(x)>f(x)-\eta $ and $-a\le f(x)$. This proves the claim. Consequently there is a continuous $g_1$ on $X$ with $|g_1|\le a$ and $|f-g_1|\le a/2$ on $F$. Applying the same construction to $f-g_1$ on $F$, we find a continuous $g_2$ with $|g_2|\le a/2$ and $|f-g_1-g_2|\le a/4$ on $F$, and inductively continuous $g_ k$ with $|g_ k|\le 2^{1-k}a$ and $|f-g_1-\cdots -g_ k|\le 2^{-k}a$ on $F$. The series $\sum _ kg_ k$ converges uniformly on $X$; its sum is continuous and equals $f$ on $F$, and clamping it to $[-a,a]$, that is, replacing it by $\max \{ -a,\min \{ a,\sum _ kg_ k\} \} $, does not change its values on $F$. $\square$ Lemma 7.5.4 . 56B45ADBA326 Let $K,L\subset D$ be compact sets with $K\subset \operatorname{Int}L$, and let $f$ be a real Borel function which is defined and quasi-continuous on a neighborhood of $L$. Then, for every $\delta >0$, \[  \operatorname {Cap}_ D^*(K\cap \{ |f|>\delta \} ) \le \operatorname {Cap}_ D(L\cap \{ |f|>\delta /2\} ).  \] Proof. Let $\eta >0$. By quasi-continuity, applied to the compact set $L$, there is an open set $G\subset D$ with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G)<\eta $ such that $f$ is continuous on $L\setminus G$; let $g$ be a continuous extension of $f|_{L\setminus G}$ to $\mathbb {C}^ n$ (lemma 7.5.3 ); here $f|_{L\setminus G}$ is bounded, being continuous on a compact set. The open set $G\cup (\operatorname{Int}L\cap \{ |g|>\delta /2\} )$ contains $K\cap \{ |f|>\delta \} $, since $K\subset \operatorname{Int}L$ and $g=f$ on $K\setminus G$. Its part outside $G$ is a Borel set contained in $L\cap \{ |f|>\delta /2\} $, because $g=f$ on $L\setminus G$. By monotonicity and subadditivity, \[  \operatorname {Cap}_ D^*(K\cap \{ |f|>\delta \} )\le \eta +\operatorname {Cap}_ D(L\cap \{ |f|>\delta /2\} ).  \] Let $\eta \downarrow 0$. $\square$ Definition 7.5.5 . DAD5D0809372 A net $(f_ a)$ of Borel functions $f_ a\colon D\to [-\infty ,+\infty ]$ converges locally in capacity to a Borel function $f\colon D\to [-\infty ,+\infty ]$ if, for every compact set $K\subset D$ and every $\delta >0$, \[  \operatorname {Cap}_ D^*(K\cap \{ f_ a>f+\delta \} )\longrightarrow 0, \qquad \operatorname {Cap}_ D^*(K\cap \{ f_ a<f-\delta \} )\longrightarrow 0.  \] Here $\pm \infty +\delta =\pm \infty $ and $\pm \infty -\delta =\pm \infty $. For finite functions, $K\cap \{ |f_ a-f|>\delta \} $ is the union of the two sets in the definition, so by monotonicity and subadditivity of outer capacity the two conditions together are equivalent to $\operatorname {Cap}_ D^*(K\cap \{ |f_ a-f|>\delta \} )\to 0$. Convergence locally in capacity is a local property: it holds on $D$ if and only if, for every ball $B\Subset D$, it holds on $B$ with $\operatorname {Cap}_ B$ in place of $\operatorname {Cap}_ D$. Indeed, if it holds on $D$ and $K\subset B$ is compact, then proposition 7.4.3 (4) gives $\operatorname {Cap}^*_ B(A)\le C\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(A)$ for all $A\subset K$. Conversely, if it holds on every ball $B\Subset D$, cover a compact set $K\subset D$ by finitely many balls $B(x_ i,r_ i)$ with $\overline{B(x_ i,2r_ i)}\subset D$; for $A\subset K_ i=K\cap \overline{B(x_ i,r_ i)}$, proposition 7.4.3 (4) gives $\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(A)\le \operatorname {Cap}^*_{B(x_ i,2r_ i)}(A)$, and subadditivity over $i$ gives the condition on $D$. In particular, for functions on an open set $W\subset D$, convergence locally in capacity with $\operatorname {Cap}_ W$ is equivalent to the same condition, for compact subsets of $W$, with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D$, since both are equivalent to the condition on balls $B\Subset W$. Proposition 7.5.6 . 9542ED69E1C1 Let $u_ j$ be locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions on $D$ decreasing to a locally bounded function $u$. Then $u_ j\to u$ locally in capacity. Moreover, a net of real Borel functions on $D$ which is uniformly bounded on each compact subset of $D$ and converges locally in capacity to a locally bounded real Borel function also converges in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(D)$. Proof. Let $K\subset D$ be compact and $\delta >0$. Since $u_ j\ge u$, the sets $\{ u_ j<u-\delta \} $ are empty, and we must show that $\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(K\cap \{ u_ j-u>\delta \} )\to 0$. By theorem 5.10.1 , $u$ is plurisubharmonic. Covering $K$ by finitely many balls $B(x,r)$ with $\overline{B(x,4r)}\subset D$ and using subadditivity of outer capacity, we may assume that $K\subset \overline{B(x,r)}$ for such a ball; put $L=\overline{B(x,3r/2)}$, $B=B(x,3r)$ and $B_1=B(x,4r)$. We first make the functions coincide near $\partial B$. Since $u\le u_ j\le u_1$, all these functions are bounded on $B_1$ uniformly in $j$, so there are constants $c$ and $N\ge 1$ with $-N\le u_ j-c,\, u-c\le -1$ on $B_1$. Put $\psi =|z-x|^2-9r^2$, choose $\delta _0>0$ with $L\subset \{ \psi <-\delta _0\} $, and let $\hat u_ j=\max \{ u_ j-c,A\psi \} $ and $\hat u=\max \{ u-c,A\psi \} $, with $A=N/\delta _0$, be the functions ( 7.3.2 ) on $B_1$, with $\delta _0$ in place of $\delta $. They are bounded and plurisubharmonic on $B_1$, $\hat u_ j\downarrow \hat u$, $\hat u_ j-\hat u=u_ j-u$ on $L$, and $\hat u_ j=\hat u$ on a collar of $\partial B$. By ( 7.4.6 ), applied with $u=\hat u$ and $h=\hat u_ j$, \[  \operatorname {Cap}_ D\bigl (B\cap \{ \hat u_ j-\hat u>\delta /2\} \bigr ) \le (n+1)!\, (2/\delta )^{n+1}\int _ B(\hat u_ j-\hat u)(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\hat u)^ n,  \] and the right-hand side tends to zero by dominated convergence, since $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\hat u)^ n$ has finite mass on $B$ and $0\le \hat u_ j-\hat u\le \hat u_1-\hat u$ decreases to zero. The real function $w_ j=u_ j-u$ is quasi-continuous on $D$, as a difference of two real quasi-continuous functions (theorem 7.5.2 and the remark following definition 7.5.1 ), and $w_ j=\hat u_ j-\hat u$ on $L$. Hence lemma 7.5.4 gives \[  \operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(K\cap \{ w_ j>\delta \} )\le \operatorname {Cap}_ D(L\cap \{ w_ j>\delta /2\} )\le \operatorname {Cap}_ D\bigl (B\cap \{ \hat u_ j-\hat u>\delta /2\} \bigr )\longrightarrow 0.  \] For the second assertion, let $f_ a\to f$ be as in the statement, let $K\subset D$ be compact, and let $M$ bound $|f_ a|$ and $|f|$ on $K$. Splitting $K$ into the Borel set where $|f_ a-f|>\delta $ and its complement, and using proposition 7.4.3 (3) together with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D\le \operatorname {Cap}^*_ D$ on Borel sets, we get \[  \int _ K|f_ a-f|\, \mathrm{d}V_{2n} \le 2MC_ D\operatorname {Cap}_ D^*(K\cap \{ |f_ a-f|>\delta \} ) +\delta |K|.  \] Taking the limit along the net and then letting $\delta \downarrow 0$ proves $L^1$ convergence on $K$. $\square$ Lemma 7.5.7 . 880C30054932 Let $B\subset \mathbb C^ n$ be a ball, and let $\mathcal U$ be a family of plurisubharmonic functions on $B$ which is uniformly bounded on each compact subset of $B$. For every compact set $K\subset B$ there is a constant $C$ such that, for all integers $0\le q\le n$, all $u_1,\ldots ,u_ q\in \mathcal U$ and all Borel sets $E\subset K$, the trace measure $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q\wedge \beta ^{n-q}$, and the total variation of every coefficient measure of $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q$, give $E$ mass at most $C\operatorname {Cap}_ B(E)$. Let $S_ j=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{1,j}\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{q,j}$ with $u_{l,j}\in \mathcal U$, and suppose that $S_ j\to S$ weakly. Let $f_ j$ be real Borel functions on $B$, uniformly bounded on each compact subset of $B$, which converge locally in capacity (for $\operatorname {Cap}_ B$) to a real Borel function $f$ that is locally bounded and quasi-continuous. Then $f_ jS_ j\to fS$ weakly, and the same holds for the trace measures of $S_ j$ and $S$. This applies in particular to a fixed weight $f_ j=f$. Proof. (1) Let $B=B(a,R)$, fix $K$, and choose $R'<R$ with $K\subset B'=B(a,R')$. Let $M\ge 1$ be a common bound for $|u|$ on $B'$, $u\in \mathcal U$. For $u_1,\ldots ,u_ q\in \mathcal U$ put $v_ l=(u_ l+M)/(2M)$ and $\phi =|z-a|^2/R'^2$; these functions take values in $[0,1]$ on $B'$, and so does \[  F=\frac1n\bigl (v_1+\cdots +v_ q+(n-q)\phi \bigr ),  \] which is therefore a competitor for $\operatorname {Cap}_{B'}$. Expand $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}F)^ n$ by additivity, positive homogeneity and symmetry (proposition 7.2.2 , theorem 7.3.7 ). All terms are positive measures, and those in which each $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ l$ occurs once and $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\phi $ occurs $n-q$ times add up to $c_{n,q}\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ q\wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\phi )^{n-q}$, where $c_{n,q}=n^{-n}\, n!\, (n-q)^{n-q}/(n-q)!>0$ (with $0^0=1$) is the corresponding multinomial coefficient. Hence $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ q\wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\phi )^{n-q}\le c_{n,q}^{-1}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}F)^ n$. Since $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\phi =\beta /(\pi R'^2)$ and $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ l=2M\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ l$, it follows that $\int _ E\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q\wedge \beta ^{n-q}\le C\operatorname {Cap}_{B'}(E)$ for Borel $E\subset B'$. The bound for the coefficient measures follows from theorem 5.3.7 , and proposition 7.4.3 (4), applied to $B'\Subset B$ and $K$, replaces $\operatorname {Cap}_{B'}$ by $\operatorname {Cap}_ B$ on subsets of $K$. (2) The weak limit $S$ is a positive current (theorem 5.3.7 ). Let $\sigma _ j$ be either the trace measure or a coefficient measure of $S_ j$, and $\sigma $ the corresponding measure of $S$; then $\int \psi \, \mathrm d\sigma _ j\to \int \psi \, \mathrm d\sigma $ for every test function $\psi $, since this integral is the value of $S_ j$ on a test form. Fix a continuous function $\chi $ with compact support in $B$ and a compact set $K\subset B$ with $\operatorname{Supp}\chi \subset \operatorname{Int}K$, and let $C$ be the constant of (1) for $K$; in particular $|\sigma _ j|(K)\le C\operatorname {Cap}_ B(K)$, which is finite by proposition 7.4.3 (1). A similar bound holds for $\sigma $ on open subsets $U\subset \operatorname{Int}K$: for the trace measure, which is the vague limit of the trace measures of $S_ j$ (section 5.3 ), proposition 2.6.2 gives $\sigma (U)\le \varliminf _ j\sigma _ j(U)\le C\operatorname {Cap}_ B(U)$, and the total variations of the coefficient measures of the positive current $S$ are bounded by a constant multiple of its trace measure. Since the total variations $|\sigma _ j|(K)$ are bounded, the convergence $\int \psi \, \mathrm d\sigma _ j\to \int \psi \, \mathrm d\sigma $ extends to continuous functions $\psi $ with support in $\operatorname{Int}K$: approximating $\psi $ uniformly by test functions supported in a fixed compact subset of $\operatorname{Int}K$ (lemma 2.5.1 (5)) changes the integrals by at most $\sup |\psi -\psi _\varepsilon |$ times a bound for $|\sigma _ j|(K)$ and $|\sigma |(K)$. Consider first the fixed weight $f$, and let $\eta >0$. Since $f$ is quasi-continuous, there is an open set $G\subset B$ with $\operatorname {Cap}_ B(G)<\eta $ such that $f$ is continuous on $K\setminus G$; let $g$ be a continuous extension of $f|_{K\setminus G}$ to $\mathbb C^ n$ with $\sup |g|\le \sup _ K|f|$ (lemma 7.5.3 ). Then \[  \Bigl |\int \chi f\, \mathrm{d}\sigma _ j-\int \chi g\, \mathrm{d}\sigma _ j\Bigr |\le 2\sup _ K|f|\sup |\chi |\, |\sigma _ j|(G\cap \operatorname{Supp}\chi )\le C'\eta ,  \] and similarly for $\sigma $, using the open set $G\cap \operatorname{Int}K$. Since $\chi g$ is continuous with support in $\operatorname{Int}K$, we have $\int \chi g\, \mathrm{d}\sigma _ j\to \int \chi g\, \mathrm{d}\sigma $. Hence $\varlimsup _ j|\int \chi f\, \mathrm{d}\sigma _ j-\int \chi f\, \mathrm{d}\sigma |\le 2C'\eta $ for every $\eta >0$, which proves $f\sigma _ j\to f\sigma $. For varying weights, let $M_ K$ bound $|f_ j|$ and $|f|$ on $K$, and let $\delta >0$. By (1), \[  \Bigl |\int \chi (f_ j-f)\, \mathrm{d}\sigma _ j\Bigr | \le \sup |\chi |\Bigl (\delta \, C\operatorname {Cap}_ B(K)+2M_ KC\operatorname {Cap}^*_ B\bigl (K\cap \{ |f_ j-f|>\delta \} \bigr )\Bigr ).  \] As $j\to \infty $, the second term tends to zero by convergence in capacity; then we let $\delta \downarrow 0$. Together with the fixed-weight case, this proves $f_ j\sigma _ j\to f\sigma $, and hence $f_ jS_ j\to fS$. $\square$ Theorem 7.5.8 . 42828E3BDDFA Let $0\le q\le n$ be an integer. For $1\le l\le q$, let $(u_{l,j})_{j\ge 1}$ be a sequence of plurisubharmonic functions on $D$, uniformly bounded on each compact subset of $D$, which converges locally in capacity to a locally bounded plurisubharmonic function $u_ l$. Then \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{1,j}\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{q,j} \longrightarrow \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q  \] weakly. More generally, if $f_ j$ are real Borel functions on $D$, uniformly bounded on each compact subset of $D$, which converge locally in capacity to a locally bounded, quasi-continuous real Borel function $f$, then $f_ j\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{1,j}\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{q,j}\to f\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q$ weakly. Proof. Weak convergence is local (lemma 7.3.6 ), so it suffices to prove the convergence on every ball $B\Subset D$. By the remark following definition 7.5.5 , the convergence in capacity holds with $\operatorname {Cap}_ B$ in place of $\operatorname {Cap}_ D$ on every ball $B\Subset D$. The limit $f$ is quasi-continuous for $\operatorname {Cap}_ B$ as well: if $K\subset B$ is compact, $K'$ is a compact neighborhood of $K$ in $B$, and $G\subset D$ is open with $f$ continuous on $K'\setminus G$, then $G\cap \operatorname{Int}K'$ is open in $B$, $f$ is continuous on $K\setminus (G\cap \operatorname{Int}K')=K\setminus G$, and $\operatorname {Cap}_ B(G\cap \operatorname{Int}K')\le C\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G)$ by proposition 7.4.3 (4) applied to $K'$. Finally, the functions $u_{l,j}$ and $u_ l$, restricted to $B$, form a family which is uniformly bounded on compact subsets of $B$. We may therefore work on such a ball and use lemma 7.5.7 . We argue by induction on $q$. For $q=0$ the product is $1$, and the weighted assertion is the second part of the lemma with $S_ j=1$. Let $q\ge 1$, and assume that $S_ j=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{2,j}\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{q,j}$ converges weakly to $S=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_2\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q$. The functions $u_{1,j}$ converge in capacity to $u_1$, which is quasi-continuous by theorem 7.5.2 ; hence the second part of the lemma gives $u_{1,j}S_ j\to u_1S$, and applying $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}$ proves the unweighted assertion for $q$ factors. The weighted assertion then follows from the second part of the lemma once more. $\square$ Unlike theorem 7.3.7 , theorem 7.5.8 concerns only products with the base current $T=1$.

title: Definition 7.5.1
text: Definition 7.5.1 . A2CACA24130B A Borel function $f\colon D\to [-\infty ,\infty ]$ is quasi-continuous (for $\operatorname {Cap}_ D$) if for every compact set $K\subset D$ and every $\varepsilon >0$ there is an open set $G\subset D$ with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G)<\varepsilon $ such that the restriction of $f$ to $K\setminus G$ is continuous. Here $[-\infty ,\infty ]$ carries its order topology.

title: Theorem 7.5.2
text: Theorem 7.5.2 . C39FEC1AB985 Let $u\in \mathrm{PSH}(D)$. For every $\varepsilon >0$ there is an open set $G\subset D$ with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G)<\varepsilon $ which contains the pole set $\{ u=-\infty \} $ and such that the restriction of $u$ to $D\setminus G$ is finite and continuous. In particular $u$ is quasi-continuous. Proof. Step 1: locally bounded $u$. Let $u$ be locally bounded, $K\subset D$ compact and $\varepsilon >0$; we find an open set $G\subset D$ with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G)<\varepsilon $ such that $u$ is continuous on $K\setminus G$. For each $x\in K$ choose $r_ x>0$ with $\overline{B(x,3r_ x)}\subset D$; finitely many balls $B(x_ i,r_{x_ i})$, $1\le i\le m$, cover $K$. Suppose that for each $i$ we find an open set $G_ i$ with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G_ i)<\varepsilon /m$ such that $u$ is continuous on $\overline{B(x_ i,r_{x_ i})}\setminus G_ i$. Then $G=\bigcup _ iG_ i$ satisfies $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G)<\varepsilon $, and $u$ is continuous on $K\setminus G$, because the finitely many sets $(K\setminus G)\cap \overline{B(x_ i,r_{x_ i})}$ are closed in $K\setminus G$ and cover it, and $u$ is continuous on each of them. We may therefore assume that $K=\overline{B'}$, where $B'=B(x,r)$, $B=B(x,2r)$ and $B_1=B(x,3r)$ satisfy $\overline{B_1}\subset D$. Subtracting a constant, we may assume that $-N\le u\le -1$ on $B_1$. Let $j>2/r$. Since $U=B(x,5r/2)$, a neighborhood of $\overline B$, lies at distance $r/2>1/j$ from $\mathbb C^ n\setminus B_1$, the regularization $u*\rho _{1/j}$ is smooth and plurisubharmonic on $U$ and takes values in $[-N,-1]$ there; moreover, $u*\rho _{1/j}$ decreases to $u$ as $j\to \infty $ (proposition 5.9.2 ). Put $\psi =|z-x|^2-4r^2$, choose $\delta >0$ with $\overline{B'}\subset \{ \psi <-\delta \} $, and let $g=\max \{ u,A\psi \} $ and $g_ j=\max \{ u*\rho _{1/j},A\psi \} $, with $A=N/\delta $, be the functions ( 7.3.2 ) on $U$. The $g_ j$ are continuous and plurisubharmonic on $U$ and decrease to $g$; moreover, $g=u$ on $\{ \psi <-\delta \} \supset \overline{B'}$, and $g_ j=g=A\psi $ on a collar of $\partial B$. For $\delta '>0$ put $G_{j,\delta '}=\{ z\in B:g_ j(z)-g(z)>\delta '\} $; it is open, because $g_ j$ is continuous and $g$ is upper semicontinuous. By ( 7.4.6 ), applied with $h=g_ j$, $u=g$ and $\delta '$ in place of $\delta $, \[  \operatorname {Cap}_ D(G_{j,\delta '})\le \frac{(n+1)!}{\delta '^{n+1}}\int _ B(g_ j-g)(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g)^ n.  \] The right-hand side tends to zero as $j\to \infty $ by dominated convergence: $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g)^ n$ has finite mass on $B$, since $g$ is bounded and plurisubharmonic near $\overline B$, and the functions $g_ j-g\ge 0$ are bounded on $B$ uniformly in $j$ and decrease to zero. Choose $j_1<j_2<\cdots $ such that $G_ l=G_{j_ l,2^{-l}}$ satisfies $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G_ l)<\varepsilon 2^{-l}$, and let $G=\bigcup _ lG_ l$.
